profiles.name: Bourbon_n_Birdies
profiles.profile: This dude is basically a wedge-and-midrange crime scene with a little bit of polish and one suspicious puddle of putting slop. The ball-striking shows up loud enough to keep him in the room, and the scoring chances are real, but the flatstick has been the one club trying to derail the party. There’s a pretty clear identity here: he can stack birdies and still leave you muttering at the scoreboard because the cleanup around the cup keeps getting weird. If the putter behaves, the whole thing gets spicy fast.

profiles.name: mikethegolfer33
profiles.tagline: BALL-STRIKING WITH A SIDE OF CHAOS
profiles.profile: This is the classic guy who flushes it enough to make the card look pretty and then adds just enough nonsense to keep the room humble. The long game has been the loud part of the profile, and the putter showed up with actual manners, but the short game is still hanging around like a bad text you meant to ignore. He can create a good round without looking tidy doing it, which is honestly very simulator-golf of him. Clean enough to scare people, messy enough to stay mortal.

profiles.name: 3_vodkas_in
profiles.tagline: ONE ROUND IS A LIE, THREE ROUNDS IS THE REAL HIM
profiles.profile: Volatile as hell, which is either a warning label or a personality trait. One appearance looked like a grown-up round with scoring, birdies, and actual touch around the greens; the others were a different species of mess, with the short game and putter taking turns lighting the place on fire. The overall file says he can absolutely pop when the wedges and lag putts cooperate, but the floor is still sitting in a ditch. In other words: dangerous upside, extremely sketchy plumbing.

profiles.name: Golfnut7413
profiles.tagline: APPROACH MERCY KILLER, SHORT GAME MENACE
profiles.profile: The irons are doing the heavy lifting here, and when they’re dialed this file looks way better than the finish column wants to admit. The problem is the chipping side keeps wandering into the traffic lane and asking for trouble, so the good tee-to-green stuff doesn’t always cash cleanly. He can absolutely build a score, but there’s enough wobble around the greens to make every promising stretch feel like it might explode at any second. Pretty good bones, slightly cursed finishing mechanics.

profiles.name: Joebat
profiles.profile: This is not a soft little slump; this is a full-scale collapse around and on the greens. The ball-striking is bad enough, sure, but the real damage comes from the short game and putting combining like two guys who should never be allowed in the same bar. The result is a card full of extra shots, extra putts, and enough self-inflicted damage to make the whole round look like a hostage situation. There’s no sugarcoating it: the swing is fighting the scorecard and the scorecard is winning by a landslide.

profiles.tagline: IRONS ON FIRE, WALKING THROUGH BROKEN GLASS
profiles.profile: This is a pure one-round scouting note, but it’s a loud one: the irons showed up with some serious juice and the putter didn’t completely sabotage the vibe. That’s enough to say the scoring gear is there when the ball-striking is humming, even if the rest of the file is still blank. The round had the feel of somebody who can manufacture birdie looks and keep the damage mostly contained. Small sample, sure, but the bones are real and the ceiling looks sneaky.
